name: The Giant Cedar of the Blijdenstein Pinetum
age_estimate: roughly 126 to 136 years, from the register's planting band of 1890-1900
access: Free, the pinetum is managed by a foundation and open to visitors.
verify_notes: LRMB register nr 1696924, registered name 'Reuzenlevensboom pineteum Blijdenstein' (Dutch 'reuzenlevensboom' = giant arborvitae, i.e. Thuja plicata, Western Red Cedar; ask the reader to confirm the exact cultivar/species since the register gives only the Dutch common name). Planting band 1890-1900, age 126-136 years. Owner category stichting (foundation), setting park, register records public visitability. Register's own history is of the PLACE: banker Benjamin Willem Blijdenstein bought 6 hectares in Hilversum on the 's-Gravelandseweg in 1880, built Villa Vogelenzang, and in 1898 had the walled fruit and vegetable garden of the estate turned into a pinetum; garden architect Hendrik Copijn designed the layout in 1909 in the English landscape style, and the path structure survives largely unchanged. This giant cedar and a giant sequoia (Sequoiadendron giganteum) date from that founding period. The villa itself was demolished in 1928 after Blijdenstein's death, but the pinetum was preserved by his will. This place-history does not itself date the individual tree beyond the register's planting band; do not bridge to a sharper date. The register is the ONE source found this pass.
